mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing wage growth and consumer spending, which in turn depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or unemployment falls below 4% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds above trend within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases the risk of stagflation and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust residential demand, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or housing starts decline below trend within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above their 12-month averages is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning; this ambiguity typically precedes equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month averages simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the contradiction resolves within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which depresses discretionary sector earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or retail sales rebound above trend within the next week.
